title: Weather, nature & seasons
goal: Talk about the weather and seasons, describe Nepal's landscape, and say what the weather is probably going to do.
intro:
Nepal rises from the hot plains of the **तराई** through the green **पहाड** (hills) to the snowy **हिमाल** — so 'the weather' depends a lot on where you are. In Nepali, rain and snow *fall* (पानी पर्छ), the sun *strikes* (घाम लाग्छ) and the wind *moves* (हावा चल्छ) — there's no dummy 'it' as in English 'it's raining'.

You'll also learn to make predictions: पानी पर्ला 'it'll probably rain', पानी पर्ने जस्तो छ 'it looks like rain'.

vocab.note: घाम लाग्यो 'the sun's out'; घाम ताप्नु 'to sunbathe (in winter)'. The sun as a body: सूर्य.
पानी पर्‍यो 'it rained'; पानी पर्दै छ 'it's raining'.
The clearest skies and the big festivals.
Used for both rain and sun.

vocab.en: to be seen, be visible; to appear
vocab.note: आज हिमाल देखिन्छ 'the mountains are visible today'.

phrases.en: It looks like it's going to rain.
In the monsoon the roads get damaged.
Which season is good for visiting Nepal?
In autumn the sky is clear.

grammar.title: Weather verbs: falls, strikes, blows
grammar.body:
Nepali weather sentences have a real subject — the rain, the sun, the wind — and a verb that goes with it:

• **पानी/हिउँ पर्छ** — rain/snow *falls*: पानी पर्‍यो 'it rained', हिउँ पर्दै छ 'it's snowing'
• **घाम लाग्छ** — the sun *strikes*: घाम लाग्यो 'the sun came out'
• **बादल लाग्छ** — clouds *strike*: बादल लागेको छ 'it's cloudy'
• **हावा चल्छ** — the wind *moves*: हावा चलिरहेको छ 'it's windy'
• **जाडो/गर्मी हुन्छ** — cold/heat *is*: आज जाडो छ 'it's cold today'

To say how **you** feel the weather, use the experiencer: **मलाई जाडो भयो** 'I'm cold', **मलाई गर्मी भयो** 'I'm hot'.

The present (पर्छ) describes what usually happens: बर्खामा धेरै पानी पर्छ 'it rains a lot in the monsoon'. The -एको छ form describes the current state: घाम लागेको छ 'the sun is out'.

examples.en: It's cloudy; you can't see the mountains.
Up there the wind blows in the evening.
In the Terai it gets very hot in summer.

examples.native: मलाई जाडो भयो, झ्याल बन्द गर।
examples.roman: malāi jāḍo bhayo, jhyāl banda gara.

grammar.title: Predictions: 'it's going to…'
grammar.body:
Nepali has several ways to talk about what the weather (or anything) is going to do:

• **-ला** (probable future): **पानी पर्ला** 'it'll probably rain', हिउँ पर्ला 'it may snow'. Very common for guesses.
• **-ने जस्तो छ** 'it looks like': **पानी पर्ने जस्तो छ** 'it looks like rain'.
• **-न लाग्यो** 'is about to / has started to': **पानी पर्न लाग्यो** 'it's starting to rain'.
• **-न सक्छ** 'may, could': हिउँ पर्न सक्छ 'it could snow'.
• **-छ रे** 'they say': भोलि पानी पर्छ रे 'they say it'll rain tomorrow'.

(The full future tense comes in unit 17.)

examples.native: आकाश हेर्नुहोस्, हिउँ पर्ने जस्तो छ।
examples.roman: ākās hernuhos, hiuṃ parne jasto chha.
examples.en: Look at the sky — it looks like snow.
They say it'll be sunny tomorrow.
There can be landslides in the monsoon.

dialogue.title: Morning at the teahouse
dialogue.setting: Tom is trekking in the Annapurna region with his guide Pemba. They check the sky over breakfast.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: पेम्बा दाइ, आज मौसम कस्तो छ?
lines.roman: Pembā dāi, āja mausam kasto chha?
lines.en: Pemba, what's the weather like today?

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: बिहान घाम लागेको छ, तर दिउँसो बादल लाग्ला।
lines.roman: bihāna ghām lāgeko chha, tara diuṃso bādal lāglā.
lines.en: It's sunny this morning, but it'll probably cloud over in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: पर्न सक्छ। माथि त हिउँ पनि पर्ला।
lines.roman: parna sakchha. māthi ta hiuṃ pani parlā.
lines.en: It could. Higher up it may even snow.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.en: Then we should leave early, right?

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: हो। सात बजे हिँडौँ। ज्याकेट र छाता बोक्नुहोस्।
lines.roman: ho. sāt baje hiṃḍauṃ. jyākeṭ ra chhātā boknuhos.
lines.en: Yes. Let's set off at seven. Bring your jacket and umbrella.

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.native: कति राम्रो! शरदमा आकाश सफा हुन्छ।
lines.roman: kati rāmro! saradmā ākās saphā hunchha.
lines.en: Beautiful! In autumn the sky is clear.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: तर कति जाडो! मेरो हात चिसो भयो।
lines.roman: tara kati jāḍo! mero hāt chiso bhayo.
lines.en: But it's so cold! My hands are freezing.

lines.speaker: Pemba
lines.en: Have some hot tea, and then let's go.

culture: Nepal is traditionally divided into three belts: **हिमाल** (the high mountains), **पहाड** (the hills, where Kathmandu and Pokhara lie) and **तराई** (the hot southern plains bordering India). The **monsoon** (बर्खा, June–September) brings rice-planting — celebrated on असार १५ with mud, rice and curd — but also landslides and leeches on the trails. Autumn (Asoj–Kattik) has clear mountain views and the biggest festivals, Dashain and Tihar. The 2015 earthquake (वि.सं. २०७२ बैशाख १२) is a shared memory: if you feel a tremor, people shout **भुइँचालो!** and run to open ground.
